answer: The cedar cap is upheld at intake and lagoon reveals the per-origin counts. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a oasis tag. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a swarm in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
